links.comparator_used: Isolated automation without data interoperability infrastructure (automation islands) and an automation-first adoption sequence, in a discrete-event simulation
links.outcome: Referral-to-treatment interval, throughput and transition volatility in simulated oncology workflows
links.effect: Fully integrated scenario: RTTI 14.9 (SD 0.3) days and capacity 1244 (SD 21.4) patients/year. Isolated automation without data infrastructure: RTTI 37.1 (SD 1.3) days (+26%) and throughput 647 (SD 10.1) patients/year. Prioritizing early interoperability reduced transition volatility compared with automation-first.
links.tradeoff: In the integrated scenario, upstream AI success shifted the binding constraint from diagnostic scanners to downstream chemotherapy infusion units. Missing interoperability led to administrative governance saturation. Results come from a simulation, not real-world data.
links.quote: Isolated automation without data infrastructure led to reduced system performance, increasing RTTI by 26% (37.1, SD 1.3 days) and reducing throughput to 647 (SD 10.1) patients per year due to administrative governance saturation.

design_hint: sequencing data interoperability before AI automation
